doc.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Getting into Gil Evans' band at the Village Vanguard
summary: Levin got the Gil Evans horn chair when the regular player went home from the Vanguard, and stayed fifteen years; he recalls the band's soloists.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Was this the same Mini Moog that I guess you took on a Gil Evans gig?
Is that right? Now what prompted you to do that?

My first stint with Gil Evans I was playing French horn, and actually got the gig, oh I’ve got a lot of stories, how much tape have you got? But that’s one of my favorites, that’s the greatest. That’s one of the three or four greatest gigs I’ve ever had. I got it — Gil was doing a week at the Village Vanguard, and the horn player was coming in from New Jersey and he came all the way into town and he forgot his mouthpiece. And he was — I think he didn’t want to do it anyways because there was a lot of work in the ‘70s. Everybody was really busy and his reaction was oh I don’t need this anyway, and he just went home. And I knew a couple of guys in the band and I got this panic call, like, “Come down to the Vanguard, now.” And I made it for the second set. And I was in the band for fifteen years.
Even back then, I don’t remember how big the band was, probably fourteen or fifteen guys in it, a lot of great soloists were in that band, guys who have been heavy influences
